title: What I learned rebuilding a Godot game with AI coding assistants and generated artwork
author: IndependentBowl7490
selftext:
I'm Kevin, an independent developer from France. I've been rebuilding D-Ops: Arcade Zombies, my Godot twin-stick shooter, using AI coding assistants and generated artwork.

The biggest challenge was making the generated assets work together inside an actual game. Perspective, character proportions, floor placement and collisions needed repeated adjustments. An attractive image didn't automatically make a readable environment.

Another lesson came from browser distribution. Platform reviewers reported first-shot lag, overlapping UI and untranslated text. Preparing graphics ahead of gameplay and testing exported builds became just as important as generating the assets.

My workflow involved directing the changes, checking the results and testing on an Android phone. AI helped with code and artwork, but the project still needed a lot of iteration.

The game is available on Android and playable in a browser:  
[https://capponuts.itch.io/d-ops-arcade-zombies](https://capponuts.itch.io/d-ops-arcade-zombies)

For others using generated assets: how do you keep perspective and scale consistent across a whole game?
